headline: Gallup finds that workers who use AI report faster and more creative work, but the gains go more often to graduates, managers and higher earners.
score_reason: Kept at 6: Gallup's own survey with large samples and stated margins of error; the findings are self-reported.
importance_line: AI's benefits at work are reaching some workers more than others, which matters first to employees without degrees or with little access to AI, then to employers and policymakers, but the findings are self-reported and Gallup says more research is needed.
summary: Gallup reports, from a survey of 7,845 US employees who use AI at work, that 63% say it helps them work faster and 56% say it helps them find more creative solutions, while 31% say it led their employer to ask them to take on more responsibility. Regular use is far more common among college graduates (40%) than among workers without a degree (17%), and Gallup notes that the findings are workers' own assessments and do not show how employers would judge the effects.
notes: Read in full. Primary source: Gallup's own release of 5 Oct 2026, first results of year two of the American Job Quality Study; full report due late Oct 2026. Survey 26 Jan to 24 Mar 2026.
